events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
This is a RydeX (non-metered) trip: the fare is a single quoted price, and the billed distance (10.8 km, exactly the optimal distance) never exceeded the optimal route, so no distance-based overcharge entered the fare [F4][F6][RD-2]. Confirming the same point, the meter/distance component is $15.17 for 10.8 km, i.e. $15.17 ÷ 10.8 km = $1.40/km on 10.8 km, so the extra 0.77 km of the off-route segment adds $0.00 to a fixed quote — the non-metered branch of RD-2 allows recovery only of ERP/toll or unpublished post-trip add-ons, and this fare contains none (base $3.90, distance $15.17, time $4.50, waiting $0.00, platform $1.47, discount $0.00) [F4][F6][RD-2].

Nevertheless the deviation itself is established: one off-route segment 14:19–14:22 drove 2.15 km where the optimal route covers 1.38 km, adding 0.77 km and reaching up to 1019 m from the optimal route, with no percentage or absolute threshold required by RD-1 [F1][F3][RD-1]. None of the exemptions apply: there is no traffic incident near the route during the trip window, and the AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY / CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY speed band 4 records (30–39 km/h, 14:02–14:36) are neither band 1 nor 2 and in any event only corroborate, so RD-4 is not satisfied [F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. No rider-requested stop appears — there were no in-app chat messages at all — and the driver's bare GPS explanation does not shift the routing duty, so RD-3 does not exempt the segment either [F7][F8][RD-3]. RD-5 also fails: no driver message proposing a route change and no rider agreement exist, and the driver's post-hoc statement is not prior consent [F7][F8][RD-5]. The segment therefore stands as an unexempted detour, i.e. a breach of the driver's RD-1 duty to take the shortest and most direct route [F3][RD-1].

Because the service is non-metered and the fare is fixed at $25.04 with no unpublished add-on, the recoverable amount under RD-2 is 0, so the outcome is no_action for the fare while the RD-1 breach is recorded [F4][F6][RD-2]. The driver profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, which this case makes a repeated breach, so a flag_account referral is required [F14][RD-6]; the profile facts are used only for that additional action, not to decide the detour [F14][RD-6].

RIDER: Your fare dispute is closed with no refund. Your trip was a RydeX fixed-quote ride, so the price stays the same no matter how far the car travelled — the billed distance matched the shortest route, and nothing was added on top of the quote. We did find that the driver took a detour and did not stay on the most direct route. That breach is now on the driver's record, and their account is being sent for review. Your account is not affected and you can keep booking as usual.

DRIVER: This dispute is closed with no refund to the rider. Their RydeX fare was a fixed quote, so the extra distance on the trip did not change what they paid — the billed distance matched the optimal route and no add-ons were charged. However, we found you took a segment that was not the shortest and most direct route, and none of the exemptions applied. This is recorded as a route-deviation breach, and because of earlier upheld cases your account is being sent to Ryde account review.
